name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)

card.summary: A blend of four testosterone esters in oil, marketed as Sustanon 250; discussed in bodybuilding circles, with no appearance trials behind it.
card.note: Prescription testosterone product; sources for this entry are thin.

quick.overview:
Sustanon is the brand name of mixed-ester testosterone injections. Sustanon 250 combines four testosterone esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three of them (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate).
The blend is intended to give a mix of faster and slower release. Little published research exists, and none examines appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: Each ester is a prodrug that is cleaved to release testosterone after intramuscular injection; shorter esters act sooner and longer ones last longer, so a blend spreads release over time.
quick.risks: As with other testosterone products, general risks include acne, sperm suppression, raised red blood cell counts and cardiovascular and prostate considerations. Testosterone is a controlled substance in many countries.

lead: Sustanon is the brand name of a family of mixed-ester testosterone injections made by Organon. Sustanon 250 is an oil solution combining four testosterone esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three of them (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate).[1][3] It is a prescription testosterone replacement product and a long-standing name in bodybuilding circles, where testosterone is discussed for its effects on muscle mass and body composition, and so on how a physique looks.[3]

The idea behind the blend is staggered release: because each ester has its own elimination half-life, one injection releases testosterone from the oil depot at several rates, a sustained but non-linear release.[3][2] Wikipedia describes the usual medical interval as every three to four weeks for Sustanon 250 and every two weeks for Sustanon 100, and notes that the product is commonly prescribed for transmasculine people undergoing masculinising hormone therapy.[3]

In controlled research Sustanon 250 has been used in a double-blind trial in older men who combined it with resistance training: the testosterone group gained more fat-free mass, lost more fat mass and showed higher muscle protein synthesis than placebo.[4][12] Other human studies used it as an experimental tool for testicular suppression and for developing anti-doping detection of testosterone esters.[8][9] No trial has examined Sustanon for cosmetic or appearance outcomes in healthy young men.

chain: Injected esters release testosterone over time
Androgen signalling raises muscle protein synthesis
More lean mass and less fat mass
angle.text: Testosterone products are used in medicine to restore levels and in bodybuilding circles to add lean mass, and a 2019 trial combining Sustanon with resistance training found larger gains in fat-free mass than placebo in older men.[4] In the looks context the payoff is a more muscular, leaner physique, alongside well-documented side effects.

paras: Sustanon is given by intramuscular injection as testosterone replacement.[3] Testosterone medicines are mainly prescribed for male hypogonadism, for masculinising hormone therapy in transgender men and transmasculine people, and in some cancer settings; Wikipedia describes the benefit of replacement for age-related low levels as unclear, and a 2020 American College of Physicians guideline favouring periodic reassessment.[2] Reviews of testosterone replacement list intramuscular Sustanon among the clinically available delivery forms, alongside gels, patches and long-acting depot injections.[5] Wikipedia reports brief UK shortages in late 2011 and mid-2012 because of manufacturing changes, during which UK health committees recommended enanthate or undecanoate alternatives.[3]

Wikipedia describes Sustanon as a popular anabolic steroid among bodybuilders during bulking phases, a statement it marks as lacking a citation.[3] Testosterone raises lean mass and strength and shapes body hair, voice and fat distribution, which is why masculinising therapy uses it and why it is taken non-medically for physique goals.[2] In T Nation threads, members compare Sustanon with other ester blends, debate how the esters behave at different injection frequencies and discuss blood-test monitoring while on testosterone.[6][7][11] This wiki does not give dosing or injection guidance.

Sustanon 250 is an oil solution for intramuscular injection that contains four testosterone esters in one product: testosterone propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate, totalling 250 mg of esters per millilitre, which is where the number in the name comes from. [3] It is made by Organon, and other names listed for the same or similar products include Sustanon Prolongatum, Durateston, Durandrone Forte and Prarbolan. A lower-strength Sustanon 100 also exists. [3]

Because the esters are released from the oil depot at different rates, the mixture is described as giving a sustained but non-linear release of testosterone, which allows dosing intervals of around three to four weeks in prescribed use. [3] Wikipedia also records short supply interruptions in late 2011 and mid-2012 linked to manufacturing changes, during which UK health committees recommended testosterone enanthate or undecanoate as alternatives. [3]

The esters are prodrugs: they are cleaved after injection to release testosterone, and their different elimination half-lives give a sustained but non-linear release from the oil depot.[3][2] Testosterone ester blends in oil are the most common injectable route for replacement therapy.[2]

Anti-doping researchers studied the detection of Sustanon esters in blood. In a six-person clinical study that included a single Sustanon injection, intact esters could be followed in serum and plasma over a 60-day sampling window, which gives a way to prove exogenous testosterone use.[8]

Testosterone itself has very low oral bioavailability because of first-pass liver metabolism, and is highly bound to sex hormone-binding globulin and albumin; injectable esters act as prodrugs that release the hormone slowly.[2] In the 2015 detection study, six participants received a single intramuscular injection of either testosterone undecanoate or a Sustanon-type mixture of four esters; all esters were detectable by LC-MS/MS in blood across the 60-day sampling window, with detection time varying by ester.[8][12]

Testosterone was first isolated in 1935 and approved for medical use in 1939 according to Wikipedia.[2] Sustanon is an Organon product, and Wikipedia lists Schering-Plough and Merck among its developers.[3] The Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 1990 put testosterone and other anabolic steroids under US controlled-substance schedules, and the 2011 and 2012 UK shortages were attributed to manufacturing changes.[2][3]

Older men and resistance training (2019). A randomized, double-blind trial in 18 healthy, non-hypogonadal men aged 65 to 75 gave Sustanon or saline injections during six weeks of resistance training. The testosterone group had greater increases in total fat-free mass (P=0.007), larger reductions in fat mass (P=0.02) and greater gains in summed strength, with muscle protein synthesis of 2.13 versus 1.34 percent per day and net protein accretion of 8.3 versus 1.9 g per day. The authors concluded that testosterone with resistance training is an effective short-term way to improve muscle mass and function in this group.[4][12]

Testicular suppression (2023). A Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism study pooled three cohorts, including six healthy young men given Sustanon. In those men testosterone, LH and the Leydig-cell marker INSL3 fell during Sustanon-induced suppression and returned to baseline afterwards.[9][12]
Detection (2015). A six-participant study followed injected esters in blood for 60 days to define detection windows for anti-doping testing.[8][12]

Animal work (2024). In rats given Sustanon at three dose levels for eight weeks, testicular size and weight, sperm count, LH and FSH decreased and histology changed, and the authors concluded it likely harms male reproductive function.[10][12]
No studies were found of Sustanon for appearance outcomes in healthy young adults.

General testosterone-therapy effects listed by Wikipedia include acne and oily skin, scalp hair loss, suppression of sperm production that can cause reversible infertility, breast tenderness or gynecomastia from conversion to oestrogen, raised hematocrit, worsened sleep apnoea and, at high doses, mood and aggression changes; possible cardiovascular and prostate effects are also listed, and pregnancy is a contraindication.[2] Injectable oil preparations can cause pulmonary oil microembolism, with cough and shortness of breath.[2] Wikipedia notes that regulators have revised testosterone labelling over time, including cardiovascular and blood-pressure warnings.[2]
Studies of Sustanon itself in healthy men report suppressed testosterone, LH and INSL3, and a 2024 rat study reports reduced sperm count and testicular size.[9][10]

Testosterone and other anabolic steroids became controlled substances in the US under the Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 1990 and are Schedule III there, Class C in the UK, and prescription-only in the EU.[2] The World Anti-Doping Agency bans testosterone, and detection approaches include testosterone-to-epitestosterone ratios, isotope-ratio testing and, for ester mixtures, blood detection of the intact esters.[2][8] The FDA stated in 2015 that benefits and safety of testosterone for age-related decline had not been established.[2]

timeline.event: US Anabolic Steroid Control Act places testosterone and other anabolic steroids under controlled-substance schedules.[2]
Brief UK Sustanon shortage after a manufacturing site change.[3]

Double-blind trial of Sustanon with resistance training in older men published.[4]
Study of INSL3, testosterone and LH during Sustanon-induced testicular suppression published.[9]
Rat study reports Sustanon suppresses spermatogenesis and increases cell death.[10]

lore.intro: Sustanon is discussed in lifting and TRT forums as a multi-ester option, with threads comparing it with other blends and asking how the esters behave over time.[6][7]

claims.claim: A multi-ester blend gives smoother, longer-lasting testosterone levels than a single ester
claims.believers: Forum users describe Sustanon as a four-component product intended to release over a long period, and compare similar blends to it.[11]
claims.experts: Pharmacology sources describe the different half-lives of the esters and the sustained but non-linear release of blends.[3]

claims.claim: Testosterone with training builds more muscle and less fat
claims.believers: Bodybuilders describe testosterone products as a route to a bigger, leaner physique.[3]
claims.experts: A double-blind trial found larger fat-free mass gains and fat-mass loss in older men given Sustanon with resistance training than in placebo.[4][12]

claims.claim: Smaller, more frequent injections work better than the standard interval
claims.believers: T Nation members ask whether Sustanon suits very frequent injections and break down weekly frequency options.[6][7]
claims.experts: The published medical schedule is every three to four weeks for Sustanon 250; no trial in the sources compares injection frequencies.[3]

claims.claim: Stopping testosterone leaves the body's own production intact
claims.believers: Some users report returning to normal after finishing.
claims.experts: Studies in healthy men show androgen treatment suppresses testosterone, LH and INSL3, with recovery to baseline in the testicular suppression study, and a rat study reports reduced sperm count.[9][10]
